source_text:
ἀκροατὴν διὰ τὸ μὴ νοεῖσθαι. ἡ δὲ προφητεία τοῖς πιστοῖς δίδοται, ἥτις περὶ τῶν
μελλόντων λαλεῖ οἷς οὐχ ὁ τυχὼν πιστεύει ἀλλ' ὁ πιστός. τὸ δὲ σημεῖον δίδοται τοῖς
ἀπίστοις, ἵνα πιστεύσῃ οἷς ὁρᾷ, ἡ δὲ προφητεία, ἵνα καταδέξηται τὸ ῥηθὲν καὶ
εὐλογήσῃ τὸν κύριον. ἄπιστον δὲ λέγει τὸν Ἕλληνα, ἰδιώτην δὲ τὸν κατηχούμενον.
ἔστι δὲ ὅπου καὶ ὁ ὀλιγόπιστος καλεῖται ἄπιστος. 270 1 Kor 14,26 Ἕκαστος δι' ἧς ἔχει
χάριτος παρὰ θεοῦ, διὰ ταύτης τὴν ἐκκλησίαν οἰκοδομείτω. 1 Kor 14,28 Εἰπὼν
σιγάτω ἐδίδαξεν ὅτι πνεύματι ἁγίῳ λαλῶν ὅτε θέλει λαλεῖ καὶ σιωπᾷ ὡς καὶ οἱ
προφῆται, οὐ μὴν οἱ κατεχόμενοι πνεύματι ἀκαθάρτῳ· ἐκεῖνοι γὰρ καὶ ὅτε οὐ
θέλουσι λαλοῦσι καὶ ἃ οὐκ ἴσασιν. 1 Kor 14,29–32 ∆ιὰ τούτων δείκνυσιν ὅτι ταῖς
ψυχαῖς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον ἀπεκάλυπτε τὰ μυστήρια, κἀκεῖναι φωτισθεῖσαι
ἀπεκάλυπτον ἀνθρώποις, οὐχ ὡς ἐν ταῖς μαντείαις οὐκ οἶδεν ὁ μάντις τί φθέγγεται.
ἀπέδωκεν οὖν ἐκεῖνο τὸ πρῶτον ὃ ἔλεγεν, ὅτι ὅτε ἦτε ἔθνη πρὸς τὰ εἴδωλα τὰ
ἄφωνα ὡς ἀνήγεσθε ἀπαγόμενοι. Προφῆται δὲ δύο ἢ τρεῖς λαλείτωσαν, οἱ ἄλλοι δὲ
διακρινέτωσαν, οἱ ἔχοντες τὸ χάρισμα τῆς διακρίσεως τῶν πνευμάτων. Ἐὰν δὲ ἄλλῳ
ἀποκαλυφθῇ καθημένῳ, ὁ πρῶτος σιγάτω, ὡς ἐν αὐτοῖς ὂν ποτὲ μὲν σιγᾶν, ποτὲ δὲ
λέγειν. καὶ πνεύματα προφητῶν προφήταις ὑποτάσσεται. μὴ φοβηθῇς, φησίν, ἐὰν
σιγήσῃς, ὡς ἀθετῶν τὸ πνεῦμα· οἶδεν γὰρ τὰ χαρίσματα ἀλλήλοις ὑποτάσσεσθαι.
∆ηλονότι οἱ ἔχοντες χαρίσματα τῆς διακρίσεως τῶν πνευμάτων. Μὴ φοβηθῇς ἐὰν
σιωπήσῃς, ὡς ἀθετῶν τὸ πνεῦμα· οἶδεν γὰρ τὰ χαρίσματα ἀλλήλοις ὑποτάττεσθαι,
ἵνα καὶ ἡ ἐκκλησία οἰκοδομὴν λάβοι καὶ ταραχὴ μὴ γίνεται πάντων ὁμοῦ
λαλούντων. 271 1 Kor 15,1–2 Οὐ ξένον, φησί, λέγω, ἀλλ' ὅπερ ἐκήρυξα. καὶ οὐχὶ ἐγὼ
μὲν ἐκήρυξα, ὑμεῖς δὲ οὐκ ἐδέξασθε, ἀλλ' ὃ καὶ παρελάβετε. καὶ οὐχὶ μάταιον
παρελάβετε καὶ ἀνόνητον, ἀλλ' ἐν ᾧ σώζεσθε. μέλλων δὲ λέγειν ὅτι ἐγνώρισα ὑμῖν
ὡς ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἀπέθανεν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, φησίν· τίνι δὲ λόγῳ τοῦτο τὸ εὐαγγέλιον,
ἵνα πιστευθῇ ἡ ἀνάστασις· ἀπαρχὴ γὰρ Ἰησοῦς τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἀποθανὼν ὑπὲρ
ἡμῶν. εἰ γὰρ μὴ ἔδει τὸν θάνατον ἀναιρεθῆναι, οὐκ ἂν ἐνηνθρώπησεν ὁ σωτήρ.
ἐκτὸς εἰ μὴ εἰκῇ ἐπιστεύσατε, ἀντὶ τοῦ πλὴν εἰ μὴ εἰκῇ ἐπιστεύσατε· ἐγὼ γὰρ λέγω
ὅτι εἰ μὴ κατέχετε, φανερὸν ὅτι εἰκῇ ἐπιστεύσατε. Ὁ λόγος τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, ἡ ἐκ
νεκρῶν ἀνάστασις ἧς ἡ ἀρχὴ ἡ τοῦ Χριστοῦ· εἰ γὰρ μὴ ἠβούλετο τὸν θάνατον
ἀναιρεθῆναι ὁ θεός, οὐκ ἂν ἐνηνθρώπησεν. εἰ οὖν μὴ κατέχετε ἃ ἠκούσατε ἀλλ'
ἀποβεβλήκατε, δῆλον ὡς εἰκῇ ἐπιστεύσατε. τὸ δὲ ἐκτὸς ἀντὶ τοῦ πλήν. 1 Kor 15,3 Τὸ
ἐν πρώτοις εἶπεν ἀντὶ τοῦ πρὸ πάντων τοῦτο ὑμῖν παρέδωκα. Ἐν πρώτοις, πρὸ
πάντων. οὐκ ἴδιον δὲ παρέδωκα ἐπιχείρημα ἀλλ' ὃ παρέλαβον ἐκ τῶν γραφῶν.
ἐπιστώθη δὲ αὐτοψίᾳ, ὅτι Χριστὸς ἀποθανὼν ἀνέστη καὶ ἐκάλεσεν αὐτὸν ἐξ
οὐρανῶν. 1 Kor 15,4 Πῶς ἐτάφη, εἰ σάρκα οὐκ εἶχεν κατὰ τοὺς αἱρετικούς; 1 Kor 15,6
Ἀντὶ τοῦ πλέον ἢ πεντακοσίοις. 272 1 Kor 15,8 Ἔκτρωμα δέ ἐστι τὸ πρὸ τοῦ
διαμορφωθῆναι καὶ λαβεῖν τὸν προσήκοντα αὐτῷ χρόνον τὸν ἐν τῇ γαστρὶ
ἐκβαλλόμενον, ὃ καὶ ζῆν οὐ δύναται. ἐπειδὴ τοίνυν ὡς ἐν γαστρὶ τὰ βρέφη
πλάττεται, ἐν τῷ νόμῳ προεμορφοῦντο αἱ ψυχαὶ πρὸς εὐσέβειαν, ἀνεγεννῶντο δὲ ἐξ
ὕδατος καὶ πνεύματος· ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἐδίωκεν τὴν ἐκκλησίαν οὐ μορφούμενος ἐν
νόμῳ εἰς τὸ τέλειον–ἐδίωκε γάρ–, διὰ τοῦτο ἔκτρωμα ἑαυτὸν ἐκάλεσεν, καὶ τοῦτο
ἑξῆς ἐπιφέρει· διότι ἐδίωξα τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ. Τὰ ἐκβαλλόμενα βρέφη πρὶν ἢ
διαμορφωθῆναι ἐν τῇ γαστρὶ ἐκτρώματα καλεῖται. ἐπεὶ οὖν ἐν μὲν τῷ νόμῳ
προεμορφοῦντο αἱ ψυχαὶ πρὸς εὐσέβειαν, ἀνεγεννῶντο δὲ ἐξ ὕδατος καὶ πνεύματος,
ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ὡς οὐ μορφωθεὶς ἐν τῷ νόμῳ ἐδίωκε τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, διὰ τοῦτο ἑαυτὸν
εἰκότως ἔκτρωμα ὀνομάζει. 1 Kor 15,9–10α Ἐλάχιστος ἐν τοῖς ἀποστόλοις, ἐπειδὴ
ἐκείνων μὴ διωξάντων ἀλλὰ πιστευσάντων ἐγὼ ἐδίωξα. Κατὰ πρόγνωσιν θεοῦ
διώκτης ὢν ἔτυχε τοσαύτης χάριτος, διὸ καὶ πλείω τῶν ἄλλων ἐκοπίασεν. 1 Kor
15,10β Οὐ μάτην ἔλαβον πολλὴν χάριν, ἀλλ' ἐχρησάμην αὐτῇ ὑπὲρ τοῦ κηρύγματος,
περισσοτέρον αὐτῶν πάντων κοπιάσας. Ἀντὶ τοῦ οὐ μάτην τὴν χάριν ἔλαβον·
κεκοπίακα γάρ. 1 Kor 15,12–13 Οὐκ ἐγχωρεῖ Χριστὸν μὲν ἀναστῆναι, τοὺς δὲ λοιποὺς
μηκέτι· ἀλλ' ὁμολογουμένως δι' οὐδὲν Χριστὸς ἀπέθανε καὶ ἀνέστη, εἰ μὴ διὰ τὴν
ἡμετέραν ἀνάστασιν. 1 Kor 15,14–18 Εἰ μὴ ἐγήγερται, φησίν, ὁ Χριστός, μάτην
pass_a_gloss: [14:21-23 second form, continued] ...the hearer because of not being understood. [Not printed again: And prophecy is given to the believers, which speaks about things to come, which not the chance person believes but the believer.] And the sign is given to the unbelievers, so that he may believe the things he sees, and the prophecy, so that he may accept the thing said and bless the Lord. [Not printed again: And he calls the Greek unbeliever, and the catechumen private person. And there is where also the one of little faith is called unbeliever.] [Page 270; label 1 Kor 14,26] Each, through the grace which he has from God, through this let him build up the church. [Label 1 Kor 14,28] Having said 'let him be silent', he taught that the one speaking by the Holy Spirit speaks when he wishes and is silent, as also the prophets, not however those possessed by an unclean spirit; for those speak even when they do not wish, and things which they do not know. [Label 1 Kor 14,29-32] Through these he shows that the Holy Spirit revealed the mysteries to the souls, and those, having been enlightened, revealed [them] to people, not as in soothsayings the soothsayer does not know what he utters. So he paid back that first thing which he was saying, that when you were nations you were led off to the voiceless idols as carried away. 'Let prophets, two or three, speak, and let the others discern', those having the gift of discernment of the spirits. 'And if [something] is revealed to another sitting, let the first be silent', as it being in them sometimes to be silent, sometimes to speak. 'And spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.' Do not fear, he says, if you are silent, as setting aside the Spirit; for the gifts know to be subject to one another. [Second form, not printed again: Clearly those having gifts of discernment of the spirits. Do not fear if you keep silence, as setting aside the Spirit; for the gifts know to be subject to one another,] [printed as an addition:] so that the church may also receive building up and confusion may not happen with all speaking together. [Page 271; label 1 Kor 15,1-2] I do not say a strange thing, he says, but what I preached. And not [that] I preached but you did not receive, but what you also received. And you did not receive [something] vain and useless, but in which you are being saved. And being about to say that 'I made known to you how the Lord Jesus died for us', he says: 'in what word' this gospel, so that the resurrection may be believed; for Jesus is firstfruits of the resurrection, having died for us. For if death did not need to be destroyed, the Savior would not have become man. 'Unless you believed in vain' instead of 'except if you believed in vain'; for I say that if you do not hold fast, it is evident that you believed in vain. [Second form, not printed again: The word of the gospel, the resurrection from the dead, of which the beginning is that of Christ; for if God did not wish death to be destroyed, he would not have become man. So if you do not hold fast what you heard but have thrown it away, it is clear that you believed in vain. And 'except' [stands] instead of 'but'.] [Label 1 Kor 15,3] He said 'in first things' instead of 'before all things I handed this on to you'. [Repeat, not printed again: In first things: before all things.] And I did not hand on my own argument, but what I received from the Scriptures. And it was confirmed by eyewitnessing that Christ, having died, rose and called him from the heavens. [Label 1 Kor 15,4] How was he buried, if he did not have flesh according to the heretics? [Label 1 Kor 15,6] Instead of 'more than five hundred'. [Page 272; label 1 Kor 15,8] An abortion is the one expelled before being fully formed and receiving the time proper to it in the womb, which also cannot live. Since then, as babies are shaped in the womb, souls were preformed in the law toward piety, and were reborn from water and Spirit; but Paul persecuted the church, not being formed in the law to completion (for he persecuted); because of this he called himself an abortion, and he brings this next: 'because I persecuted the church of God.' [Second form, not printed again: The babies expelled before being fully formed in the womb are called abortions. Since then in the law souls were preformed toward piety, and were reborn from water and Spirit, but Paul, as not formed in the law, persecuted the church, because of this he fittingly names himself an abortion.] [Label 1 Kor 15,9-10a] Least among the apostles, since while they did not persecute but believed, I persecuted. Being a persecutor according to God's foreknowledge he obtained such great grace, therefore he also labored more than the others. [Label 1 Kor 15,10b] I did not receive much grace in vain, but I used it for the preaching, having labored more abundantly than all of them. [Second form, not printed again: Instead of 'I did not receive the grace in vain; for I have labored.'] [Label 1 Kor 15,12-13] It is not possible for Christ to rise, but the rest no longer; but admittedly Christ died and rose for nothing except for our resurrection. [Label 1 Kor 15,14-18] If Christ has not been raised, he says, in vain... [continues]
pass_b_english: …hearer, because it is not understood. The sign is given to unbelievers, so that they may believe what they see; prophecy is given so that one may accept what was said and bless the Lord.
On 1 Corinthians 14:26: Let each one build up the church through whatever grace he has from God.

On 1 Corinthians 14:28: By saying “let him be silent,” he taught that one who speaks by the Holy Spirit speaks when he wishes and keeps silent when he wishes, as the prophets did. Not so those possessed by an unclean spirit: they speak even when they do not wish to, and say things they do not know.

On 1 Corinthians 14:29–32: By these words he shows that the Holy Spirit revealed the mysteries to souls, and they, once enlightened, revealed them to men. It was not as in soothsaying, where the soothsayer does not know what he is uttering. So he has now made good what he said at the start: that when you were Gentiles, you were led away to the dumb idols, carried off as you were. “Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge”: those who have the gift of discerning spirits. “If something is revealed to another who is sitting, let the first be silent,” since it lies with them at one time to be silent and at another to speak. “And the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.” Do not be afraid, he says, that by falling silent you are slighting the Spirit, for the gifts know how to yield to one another.
The second catena form adds that this is so that the church may be built up and there may be no confusion from everyone speaking at once.

On 1 Corinthians 15:1–2: I am not telling you anything strange, he says, but what I preached. And it is not that I preached and you did not accept it: you received it. Nor did you receive something empty and useless, but that in which you are being saved. Since he is about to say, “I made known to you how the Lord Jesus died for us,” he says, “in what word”: this gospel, given so that the resurrection may be believed, for Jesus, who died for us, is the firstfruits of the resurrection. If death did not have to be destroyed, the Savior would not have become man. “Unless you believed in vain” stands for “except if you believed in vain.” For I say that if you do not hold it fast, it is plain that you believed in vain.

On 1 Corinthians 15:3: He said “first of all” meaning “before everything else”: I handed this on to you. I did not hand on an argument of my own, but what I received from the Scriptures. It was confirmed to him by his own eyes that Christ died and rose, and Christ called him from heaven.
On 1 Corinthians 15:4: How was he buried, if, as the heretics say, he did not have flesh?
On 1 Corinthians 15:6: “Above five hundred” means “more than five hundred.”

On 1 Corinthians 15:8: An untimely birth is what is expelled from the womb before it has been fully formed and has had its proper time there, and it cannot live. Just as babies are shaped in the womb, souls were shaped beforehand under the law toward godliness, and were born again of water and Spirit (John 3:5). Paul, though, persecuted the church without being shaped to completion under the law; he was persecuting it. That is why he called himself an untimely birth, and he adds next, “because I persecuted the church of God.”

On 1 Corinthians 15:9–10a: “The least of the apostles,” because they did not persecute but believed, while I persecuted. He was a persecutor, and yet by God's foreknowledge he obtained so great a grace; that is why he also labored more than the others.
On 1 Corinthians 15:10b: I did not receive great grace for nothing. I used it for the preaching, and labored more abundantly than all of them.
On 1 Corinthians 15:12–13: It cannot be that Christ rose and the rest do not. It is agreed that Christ died and rose for no other reason than our resurrection.
On 1 Corinthians 15:14–18: If Christ has not been raised, he says, in vain…

choices.english: “Above five hundred” means “more than five hundred.”
choices.why: ἀντὶ τοῦ glosses Paul's ἐπάνω πεντακοσίοις; the lemma word is supplied in quotation marks so the gloss makes sense.
Plain English for a birth before full formation; Severianus defines it in the next words.

choices.term: τίνι δὲ λόγῳ τοῦτο τὸ εὐαγγέλιον
choices.english: “in what word”: this gospel, given so that the resurrection may be believed
choices.why: Severianus picks up Paul's τίνι λόγῳ and states its purpose; kept close.
Subject is Christ, object Paul (the Damascus call).

choices.english: first form printed; second form only where it adds

bible_refs.note: διότι ἐδίωξα τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ (Severianus attaches it to 15:8)
